calls.reason: ARC Prize reported that o3 still failed very easy novel tasks despite its breakthrough scores. GSM-Symbolic found sensitivity to small problem changes, supporting the central claim of unreliable generalization.

SimpleQA found recurring factual errors and overstated confidence; GSM-Symbolic found large math accuracy drops from irrelevant clauses. These support the recurring failure pattern, although they do not establish everyday error rates.

The discussed prompt inventory and replications are missing. GSM-Symbolic tests different tasks, while MisguidedAttention reports strong o1 performance on a related collection; neither settles robustness across the specified variations.

Nature documents plausible errors and persistent variability, while Anthropic reports 64% coding success. Neither measures whether trustworthy answers are rare across ordinary uses, and the broader wording remains subjective.
